# Target under verification

A Node.js ESM port of a Python script lives in /output:
  /output/test14.mjs                 entry point
  /output/lib/*.mjs                  python-semantics helpers (pyint, pyrepr, pystr, pyunicode, pybytes, pyprint, pytraceback, pyerrors)
  /output/lib/base58/*.mjs           base58 port (alphabet, scrub, int_codec, index)
  /output/lib/argparse/*.mjs         argparse port (parser, formatter, types, exit, index)

The original Python source is /workspace/dataset/test14.py. In essence:
  parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
  parser.add_argument('--b', type=int, required=True)
  parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
  encoded_int1 = base58.b58encode_int(args.a)
  encoded_int2 = base58.b58encode_int(args.b)
  decoded_int  = base58.b58decode_int(args.c)
  print(encoded_int1); print(encoded_int2); print(decoded_int)

The GROUND TRUTH is the precompiled reference binary:
  /workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a <int> --b <int> --c <str>
Run the binary directly. NEVER use the 'python' command. ALWAYS wrap invocations
in 'timeout 10' (some inputs legitimately never terminate -- see below).

Run the port as: node /output/test14.mjs <args...>

# Differential harness (already written and validated -- prefer it)

  /tmp/dt/diff1.sh [--stderr] -- <args...>

It runs both programs with timeouts, compares stdout and exit code (and stderr
with --stderr, filtering the PyInstaller '[PYI-...' bootloader line), then prints
PASS or a FAIL block with both sides quoted via printf %q. Exit 0 = match.
Read it before use. You may write your own additional drivers under /tmp/<your-own-unique-dir>/.

# Behaviour already established by black-box probing (treat as known-correct)

base58:
- b58encode_int(0) -> b'1'  (the library's default_one behaviour, not positional arithmetic)
- alphabet: 123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz  (no 0 O I l)
- b58decode_int right-strips its argument FIRST (trailing whitespace is padding),
  THEN ascii-encodes it, THEN folds digits. So '5Q ' -> 255, '' -> 0, '   ' -> 0.
- rstrip's whitespace set is Python str.isspace() = Unicode White_Space PLUS U+001C..U+001F.
- leading/interior whitespace is NOT stripped -> ValueError: Invalid character ' '
- any character > U+007F -> UnicodeEncodeError, exit 1
- invalid ascii base58 char -> ValueError: Invalid character 'X', exit 1
- on ANY decode error stdout is completely EMPTY (nothing prints until all three values exist)

int() conversion for --a/--b:
- accepts Unicode decimal digits of any script ('١٠', '１０' -> 10), leading/trailing
  Unicode White_Space, a leading + or -, and single underscores BETWEEN digits
- REJECTS U+001C..U+001F and U+FEFF as leading whitespace (they are not White_Space)
- rejects '0x10', '10.5', '1__0', '_10', '10_', '', '²'
- argparse then reports: argument --a: invalid int value: <repr of the ORIGINAL text>, exit 2

argparse:
- missing required options are reported BEFORE unrecognized ones (so '-a 5 -b 5 -c A',
  which uses undefined short flags, complains that --a/--b/--c are missing)
- -h/--help prints help to STDOUT and exits 0, even when required options are absent
- '--he' abbreviates to --help
- '--a=5' works; '--c -A' -> 'argument --c: expected one argument'; '--c=-A' assigns '-A'
- a trailing bare '--' becomes 'unrecognized arguments: --'
- later occurrences win: '--a 5 --a 7' uses 7
- error exit status is 2; usage line goes to stderr

Arbitrary precision is required: --a values of hundreds of digits must encode exactly.

# KNOWN AND ACCEPTED deviations -- DO NOT report these, they are settled

1. Program name in usage/help/error text. The reference binary says 'test14_executable';
   the port says 'test14.mjs', derived from basename(argv[1]) exactly as Python derives
   prog from basename(sys.argv[0]). This is the intended faithful behaviour.
2. The '[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script' bootloader line. It is a PyInstaller
   launcher artifact with a per-run pid and is intentionally not reproduced.
3. Negative --a/--b never terminate in EITHER program. The library loops 'while i:' with
   floored divmod, and divmod(-1,58) == (-1,57) forever. The port reproduces the same
   non-termination on purpose. Only report a defect here if the port terminates quickly
   with output or a Node error while the reference binary hangs, or vice versa -- i.e. a
   genuine behavioural divergence, not the shared hang itself.
4. Bytes that are invalid UTF-8 in argv. Python applies surrogateescape; Node substitutes
   U+FFFD. Both still fail with exit 1. Platform-level, unfixable in pure JS.

# Hard requirements the port must satisfy (violations ARE defects)

- ESM only: 'import'/'export'. Any require() or module.exports is a violation.
- Every generated file uses the .mjs suffix, and every relative import includes it.
- ZERO external/npm dependencies. Only node: builtins and local ./ imports.
- The code must NOT use or even mention Uint8Array or Buffer anywhere. Manual base58
  logic on strings/BigInt/plain arrays only. Grep for these identifiers.
  (TextEncoder/atob/btoa-style byte APIs should also be absent.)
- No embedded or shelled-out Python.


A differential fuzzer working on "output-format-and-exit" claims this divergence between the
reference binary and the Node port:

  repro:     for i in $(seq 1 12); do timeout 10 node /output/test14.mjs --a 10000 --b 262631383 --c 5Q 2>/tmp/e3 | head -1 >/dev/null; printf '%s ' "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"; done; echo; head -6 /tmp/e3; for i in $(seq 1 12); do timeout 10 /workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a 10000 --b 262631383 --c 5Q 2>/dev/null | head -1 >/dev/null; printf '%s ' "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"; done; echo
  stream:    exitcode+stderr
  reference: Exit code 0 on all 12 runs, stderr empty. CPython block-buffers stdout when it is not a tty, so all three lines leave in a single write() that head consumes before exiting; no EPIPE is ever observed.
  port:      Exit code 1 on roughly 8-11 of 12 runs (nondeterministic race; run the loop, do not judge on a single invocation) and stderr gets a raw Node crash dump: "node:events:495 / throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event / Error: write EPIPE / at afterWriteDispatched (node:internal/stream_base_commons:160:15) ... at pyPrint (file:///output/lib/pyprint.mjs:16:18)" followed by "Node.js v18.19.1". Root cause: /output/lib/pyprint.mjs does one process.stdout.write per print with no 'error' handler, so head -1 closing the pipe after the first line makes writes 2 and 3 raise EPIPE. Same divergence with 'head -2' and with '| true' (ref rc=0, port rc=1). Also seen on the stderr side: 'node /output/test14.mjs --a x --b 1 --c A 2>&1 >/dev/null | head -1' gives rc=1 on ~9/12 runs where the reference gives 2 (the reference is itself racy there, occasionally 120, but never 1).

Your job is to REFUTE it. Actually run both programs yourself, several times and with
byte-level comparison (od -c) where output framing matters. Consider that the claim may
be an artifact of the fuzzer's own harness: shell quoting, command substitution stripping
trailing newlines, a missing timeout, locale, or the working directory (the reference
binary prints a traceback source line only when test14.py is readable from cwd).
Also check it is not one of the KNOWN AND ACCEPTED deviations.

Set real=false unless you personally reproduced a true divergence. Default to
real=false when uncertain. If it is real but described inaccurately, set real=true and
give a corrected summary. Include the actual observed output as reproEvidence.
Do NOT edit any file under /output.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential runner: compares the Node port against the reference binary.
# Usage: ./diff1.sh [--stderr] -- <args...>
# Prints PASS or a detailed FAIL block. Exit 0 on match, 1 on mismatch.
PY=/workspace/dataset/test14_executable
JS="node /output/test14.mjs"
CHECK_STDERR=0
if [ "$1" = "--stderr" ]; then CHECK_STDERR=1; shift; fi
if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then shift; fi

pout=$(timeout 10 $PY "$@" 2>/tmp/pyerr.$$); prc=$?
perr=$(cat /tmp/pyerr.$$); rm -f /tmp/pyerr.$$
jout=$(timeout 10 $JS "$@" 2>/tmp/jserr.$$); jrc=$?
jerr=$(cat /tmp/jserr.$$); rm -f /tmp/jserr.$$

ok=1
[ "$pout" != "$jout" ] && ok=0
[ "$prc" != "$jrc" ] && ok=0
if [ $CHECK_STDERR = 1 ]; then
  # Strip the PyInstaller bootloader line, whose embedded pid varies per run.
  pe=$(printf '%s' "$perr" | grep -v '^\[PYI-')
  [ "$pe" != "$jerr" ] && ok=0
fi

if [ $ok = 1 ]; then
  echo "PASS $(printf '%q ' "$@")"
else
  echo "FAIL args=$(printf '%q ' "$@")"
  echo "  py  rc=$prc stdout=$(printf '%q' "$pout")"
  echo "  js  rc=$jrc stdout=$(printf '%q' "$jout")"
  if [ $CHECK_STDERR = 1 ]; then
    echo "  py  stderr=$(printf '%q' "$(printf '%s' "$perr" | grep -v '^\[PYI-')")"
    echo "  js  stderr=$(printf '%q' "$jerr")"
  fi
  exit 1
fi

content.text:
I could not refute this. It reproduces deterministically, and I ruled out every harness-artifact hypothesis.

**What I verified:**

1. **Not a content bug** — with stdout fully consumed, both sides are byte-identical (`od -c`: `b'3yR'\n b'QD4AJ'\n 255\n`) and `diff1.sh --stderr` PASSes.

2. **`| head -1` is deterministic, not a race** — 30/30 runs: reference rc=0, port rc=1. The fuzzer's "8-11 of 12, nondeterministic" understates it. The race only appears with `head -2` (port 6/8 rc=1). With `head -3` (full drain) both are rc=0.

3. **Reference stderr is genuinely empty** — 0 bytes *before* PYI filtering, so accepted deviation #2 is not involved. The port emits 937 bytes of raw Node crash dump naming its own internal path.

4. **Ruled out artifacts** — reproduces with no `timeout` wrapper at all; reproduces from cwd `/workspace/dataset` (where `test14.py` is readable); no command substitution involved; `PIPESTATUS[0]` usage is correct. Also reproduces with `sed 1q` and `head -c 3`, and with `| true` (ref rc=0, port rc=1).

5. **Root cause confirmed** — `grep` over all of `/output` finds **zero** `'error'` handlers, no `EPIPE` handling, no `uncaughtException`. The two vulnerable sites are `/output/lib/pyprint.mjs:16` (`process.stdout.write` — one syscall per `print`, where CPython block-buffers all three lines into a single write at exit) and `/output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs:50-51` (two separate `process.stderr.write` calls).

6. **The stderr side is also deterministic** — on a clean 40-run sample, `2>&1 >/dev/null | head -1` gives ref=2 on 40/40 and port=1 on 40/40. (An earlier sample under load showed ref=120 occasionally, so the reference can be racy there, but never 1.) Without a pipe both correctly give rc=2 with matching text.

7. **Not a known accepted deviation** — it is not prog-name, not the PYI line, not the negative-value hang, not invalid-UTF-8 argv.

Notably, even the reference's *own* broken-pipe path (`| true` → `BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe` / `Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' ...>`) looks nothing like the port's `Unhandled 'error' event ... Node.js v18.19.1`, so the port diverges under every early-reader-close scenario.

Refutation attempts that all failed:
- Content/framing: with stdout fully drained the two programs are byte-identical (od -c) and diff1.sh --stderr PASSes. So it is purely an early-reader-close (EPIPE) divergence, not a wrong-output bug.
- "It's the fuzzer's race": false. For `| head -1` the port returns 1 on 30/30 runs and the reference returns 0 on 30/30. The nondeterminism the fuzzer described only exists for `head -2` (port 6/8 rc=1, ref 0/8). With `head -3` (full drain) both are 0.
- "Missing timeout": reproduces identically with no `timeout` wrapper.
- "cwd / traceback source line": reproduces from cwd=/workspace/dataset where test14.py is readable.
- "Shell quoting / command substitution stripping newlines": no command substitution is involved in the exit-code measurement; PIPESTATUS[0] is the correct index for the first pipeline element.
- "Accepted deviation #2 (PYI bootloader line)": not applicable. I captured the reference's stderr symmetrically and it is 0 bytes even BEFORE the ^\[PYI- filter, while the port emits 937 bytes. None of the four accepted deviations (prog name, PYI line, negative-value hang, invalid-UTF-8 argv) cover this.
- "Only one exotic consumer": reproduces with `head -1`, `head -c 3`, `sed 1q`, and `| true`. (`grep -m1 .` drains the pipe, so both give 0.)

Root cause verified by inspection: `grep -rn "EPIPE|on('error'|uncaughtException|unhandledRejection"` over /output/**/*.mjs returns nothing — the port installs no 'error' handler on either standard stream. /output/lib/pyprint.mjs:16 does one `process.stdout.write` per print, whereas CPython block-buffers stdout when it is not a tty and emits all three lines in a single write at exit; so the reader can close between the port's writes 1 and 2. The same defect exists on stderr at /output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs:50-51, which does two separate `process.stderr.write` calls (usage, then the error message).

Both halves of the claim are correct in direction; the fuzzer's description is inaccurate only about determinism (it is deterministic for head -1, not 8-11/12) and about the stderr-side frequency (I measured 40/40, not ~9/12). Worth noting the reference's own broken-pipe path (`| true` -> BrokenPipeError / "Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper ...>", rc=0) still bears no resemblance to the port's "Unhandled 'error' event ... Node.js v18.19.1", rc=1, so the port diverges under every early-close scenario, not just this one.
input.correctedSummary:
Neither standard stream in the port has an 'error' handler, so any consumer that closes the pipe early turns a clean exit into a Node crash dump with exit code 1.

Deterministic (not racy) on both streams:

1. stdout: `node /output/test14.mjs --a 10000 --b 262631383 --c 5Q | head -1` -> port rc=1 on 30/30 runs plus 937 bytes of raw Node crash dump on stderr; reference rc=0 on 30/30 runs with stderr completely empty (0 bytes even before PYI filtering). Cause: /output/lib/pyprint.mjs:16 issues one process.stdout.write per print, while CPython block-buffers non-tty stdout and emits all three lines in a single write at exit, so `head` never closes the pipe mid-stream on the reference. Also reproduces with `sed 1q`, `head -c 3`, and `| true`. `head -2` is the only genuinely racy variant (port ~6/8 rc=1); `head -3` (full drain) matches at rc=0.

2. stderr: `node /output/test14.mjs --a x --b 1 --c A 2>&1 >/dev/null | head -1` -> port rc=1 on 40/40 runs, reference rc=2 on 40/40 (the reference can occasionally yield 120 under load, but never 1). Cause: /output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs:50-51 makes two separate process.stderr.write calls (usage line, then the error line); `head -1` consumes the usage line and exits, so the second write raises EPIPE.

Fix: attach an 'error' handler (swallowing EPIPE) to process.stdout and process.stderr, or emulate CPython's block buffering by accumulating output and issuing a single write. Not a harness artifact: reproduces with no `timeout` wrapper, from cwd=/workspace/dataset, and with no command substitution involved. Not covered by any of the four accepted deviations.
